maria.dev: Quick heads-up — I hit a goroutine leak in the Go generator streaming example when cancelling via ctx.Done(). Posting a tiny repro below.

maria.dev: Repro steps: start stream, cancel ctx after first token, observe goroutine count spike. This only happens with generator streaming, not plain chat.

maria.dev: Snippet:```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
defer cancel()
stream, err := client.Generator().Stream(ctx, req)
if err != nil { return err }
go func() { time.Sleep(50 * time.Millisecond); cancel() }()
for {
  tok, err := stream.Recv()
  if err != nil { break }
  fmt.Println(tok.Text)
}
```

jonathan: ugh. did you use the latest sdk? we changed the stream impl last week.

maria.dev: yes, go v0.11.2 from the example module in repo.

kevin: can you paste the error or goroutine stack dump? leak might be blocked on internal recv loop.

maria.dev: no panic, just goroutines stuck in runtime.select on channel read. stack shows something inside internal stream.actorLoop() waiting on a send.

li-ml: known-ish pattern: if the client write path doesn't observe ctx cancellation, the transport goroutine can block sending into the consumer channel. We added a TODO to the runtime but maybe not fixed for generator streams.

jonathan: sounds like two issues: 1) generator.Stream API ergonomics around cancellation (should expose Close/Cancel on stream object) and 2) docs + sample app that demonstrate correct cancellation pattern.

kevin: agree. current pattern expects user to cancel ctx, but stream.Recv() doesn't always return quickly if internal buffer is full. We could make Recv return context.Canceled immediately when ctx is done and drain internal senders.

maria.dev: Minimal UX ask: update sample app to show `defer stream.Close()` or `stream.Cancel()` and show proper ctx usage. Right now docs only show a blocking loop. New users easily leak resources.

li-ml: implementation wise we can: a) add stream.Close() that atomically closes consumer channel and signals producers, b) make Recv check ctx every iteration. Both are small changes.

jonathan: +1 to adding Close(). Also add an example in README with a cancel goroutine and `for { tok, err := stream.Recv(ctx) }` variant. We should also ensure auth retries don't re-spawn a producer after Cancel.

kevin: good catch re retries — if auth refresh kicks in, it may restart background pump. Need idempotent cancel guard.

deploy-bot: @here deployment queued: update/sdk-gen-stream-fix -> staging at 2026-03-22T15:40:00Z :rocket:

maria.dev: I'd be happy to draft the sample update and a short issue with stack dump. assigning to kevin to own runtime fix.

kevin: I will open PR for Close() + Recv(ctx) check. will also add a unit test that cancels mid-stream and asserts zero leaked goroutines.

jonathan: please link the sample PR here when ready. also add a changelog note — this is a breaking-but-not-really ergonomics improvement.

maria.dev: thanks all. I'll add the example and the reproducer to the devex sample apps repo.

kevin: timeline: PR by EOD tomorrow, staging test, then merge.

maria.dev: sweet. tagging this thread for follow-up after PR: @kevin @jonathan @li-ml
